contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists (class warning): severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions are reported in anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Olanzapine was given for two doses and stopped.
interactions: IVIG + ethinyl estradiol (combined oral contraceptive): additive thrombotic risk, increased further by immobility; consider holding the contraceptive and give VTE prophylaxis.
Methylprednisolone + metformin: high-dose corticosteroids raise blood glucose; monitor capillary glucose during the pulse.
Methylprednisolone + albuterol: both lower serum potassium; check potassium during treatment.
Aciclovir IV: crystal nephropathy risk; keep well hydrated and monitor creatinine; hold metformin if renal function falls.
Lorazepam + levetiracetam: additive sedation; monitor consciousness and breathing.

output.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDAR encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in exposed patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

output.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumour removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:64); sodium 137 mmol/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies and other neuronal antibodies negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the reviewed serum work-up, including a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay that must be interpreted with CSF rather than alone
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, toxic and infective mimics and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which is read with the CSF assay.

action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.rationale: CSF anti-GluN1 IgG on a cell-based assay is the decisive test for definite disease, and HSV PCR addresses the can't-miss infectious mimic.

action_criteria.rationale: Staring spells with right arm posturing, dyskinesias and drowsiness need an EEG to separate seizures from movements; an abnormal EEG supports the diagnosis.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges); monitor capillary glucose during the steroid pulse (metformin for PCOS).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynaecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.

Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for autonomic instability (heart rate 60 to 140 bpm, blood pressure to 185/102 mmHg, diaphoresis) and recurrent seizures, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first; do not restart olanzapine, and monitor CK and temperature.
Give pharmacological VTE prophylaxis while she is bed-bound, and hold the combined oral contraceptive during the acute admission (immobility and IVIG add to its thrombotic risk).
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioural management; gynaecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1 and HSV-2 PCR negative on an LP more than 72 hours after onset; MRI medial temporal FLAIR signal is symmetric, without haemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX, IgLON5) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.
Generalized and focal seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, extreme delta brush and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands are not explained by a psychiatric disorder.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced movement disorder or neuroleptic malignant syndrome (olanzapine)
differential.key_features: Only two doses of olanzapine, stopped about 5 days before admission; dyskinesias kept worsening after it was stopped; CK 252 U/L, temperature 38.4 C and cogwheel wrist rigidity with continuous hyperkinetic movements, not the akinetic rigidity and markedly raised CK of NMS; urine drug screen negative.
ANA only 1:80 with no rash, arthritis, cytopenia or other systemic feature; a mother with SLE does not change this; CSF anti-GluN1 explains the syndrome.

key_clinical_evidence: Subacute onset over about two weeks, after a viral-like prodrome, of suspiciousness and psychosis, reduced speech with paraphasias, focal and generalized seizures, orofacial dyskinesias with chorea and dystonia, drowsiness and autonomic instability: all six of the Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:256) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:64 is read with the CSF.

MRI shows symmetric bilateral medial temporal and subtle cingulate FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and excludes structural causes, while the negative CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV encephalitis.
EEG shows extreme delta brush with left temporal electrographic seizures; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 1.9 cm left ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumour removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Viral-like prodrome (headache, low-grade fever, body aches, fatigue) preceding the neuropsychiatric syndrome.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a primary viral encephalitis (HSV) or post-viral psychosis; tempts the agent to commit to empiric antiviral therapy without pursuing autoimmune workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, dysautonomia, an abnormal EEG and CSF pleocytosis accompany the psychiatric features and require exclusion of autoimmune encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (suspiciousness, talking to herself, insomnia) diagnosed as a first episode of psychosis at urgent care, in a student with no psychiatric history.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NMS produces markedly raised CK with akinetic lead-pipe rigidity after antipsychotic exposure; a CK of 252 U/L here, days after two doses of olanzapine, reflects the seizures and continuous dyskinesias and does not change management.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Two doses of olanzapine do not explain orofacial dyskinesias that keep worsening after the drug is stopped, together with seizures and dysautonomia; the exposure is a reason not to restart an antipsychotic, not an explanation of the syndrome.
red_herrings.data_point: Orofacial dyskinesias first noticed after two doses of olanzapine and attributed by her mother to the new medication.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attributes the movement disorder to an antipsychotic side effect and delays the encephalitis work-up.

patient.history_present_illness: This 19-year-old right-handed African American woman is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after her university roommate called 911 for a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure. According to her roommate and her mother, who has been staying with her for the past week, the patient began acting strangely approximately two and a half weeks ago. She initially developed what appeared to be a mild flu-like illness with headache, low-grade fever, body aches, and fatigue lasting three to four days. She seemed to recover but then began exhibiting personality changes that her roommate described as completely out of character. She became unusually suspicious of friends, accused her roommate of going through her belongings, and withdrew from social activities. She stopped attending classes and was found by her roommate talking to herself in their shared room on multiple occasions. Her mother was contacted approximately one week ago because the roommate was concerned. Her mother drove up and noted that her daughter appeared confused, was sleeping only two to three hours per night, and had difficulty remembering recent conversations. The mother took her to a campus urgent care clinic six days ago, where she was evaluated by a physician assistant who suspected a first episode of psychosis and prescribed olanzapine 5 mg nightly. The patient took two doses but her condition continued to worsen. She developed involuntary repetitive lip-smacking and tongue movements that her mother initially attributed to the new medication. Four days prior to this presentation, she had her first witnessed seizure at home, described as whole-body stiffening followed by rhythmic jerking of all extremities lasting roughly two minutes. EMS was called and she was taken to a local community hospital where a non-contrast CT head was normal and basic labs were unremarkable aside from a sodium of 133 mEq/L. She was given levetiracetam 500 mg IV and discharged with instructions to follow up with neurology. Over the following days, the dyskinesias persisted and worsened despite discontinuation of olanzapine. She became increasingly confused and had two more seizure-like episodes characterized by staring and right arm stiffening. Today she had a prolonged generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately three minutes, prompting the current presentation to this tertiary academic medical center emergency department.

neurological_exam.additional: Prominent continuous orofacial dyskinesias with stereotyped lip-smacking and chewing movements. Choreiform movements of bilateral upper extremities, more pronounced on the right. Episodic autonomic instability manifested by heart rate fluctuations between 60 and 140 bpm during the encounter, diaphoresis, and one episode of transient hypertension to 185/102 mmHg. Three discrete episodes of behavioral arrest with subtle right arm tonic posturing lasting 10-20 seconds were observed, highly suspicious for subclinical seizures.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive at 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements conjugate without nystagmus. Corneal reflexes intact bilaterally. Facial sensation intact to noxious stimuli symmetrically. Prominent orofacial dyskinesias with repetitive lip-smacking, tongue protrusion, and chewing movements are near-continuous. Hearing grossly intact to voice. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength intact. Tongue midline when briefly protruded.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Patient is drowsy but arousable to voice, oriented only to self. She is unable to state the date, month, year, or current location. Speech is markedly reduced in fluency with frequent paraphasic errors and perseveration. She intermittently becomes agitated and attempts to remove her IV lines. She is unable to follow two-step commands. Attention is severely impaired; she cannot spell WORLD backward or perform serial 7s. Short-term memory is non-testable as she cannot register three words. Intermittent episodes of staring with lip-smacking and subtle right arm posturing are observed, lasting 10-20 seconds each.

Intermittent dystonic posturing of the right hand with wrist flexion and finger extension. neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, patellar 3+ bilaterally, Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Bilateral plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Withdraws briskly and symmetrically to noxious stimuli in all four extremities. Detailed sensory examination not possible due to altered mental status.
